summary: Most of the report holds up: prices, page quotes, per-page tag counts and DataForSEO figures match the evidence, and inferred claims carry fair confidence. The errors cluster in the ad and intent sections: LinkedIn's 9 library ads are called 'live' though the data has no active status and the screenshot shows a past-event ad and a jobs ad, the Meta page is called verified when collected.json says verified: false, and Clearbit visitor identification is counted on 7 pages when the network log shows 6. A few seen claims also carry interpretation (primary conversion, the booking-link explanation for Google, sales use of Clearbit).

items.reason: Mostly matches the claims (per-seat pricing, free plan, Enterprise from $15k/yr on pricing.md; Marketo/Clearbit/G2/LinkedIn in the stack). Two phrases state more than the evidence: 'LinkedIn is the only ad library with live Calendly ads' (collected.json ads.linkedin has status 'found' and adsMatchingSearch '9' with no active flag or run dates, and ads/linkedin.jpg shows one of the ads promoting a 'June 18, 2026' event and another a jobs ad), and 'the site is under active Statsig experimentation', which is an inference from the SDK loading, written as fact.
items.fix: Calendly sells scheduling software with an AI notetaker, an email scheduling assistant (Callie) and payments, priced per seat with a free plan and a sales-led Enterprise tier from $15k a year. Its marketing in this capture runs on brand-led organic search, free signup on nearly every page, and a B2B demand-generation stack (Marketo, Clearbit, G2 intent, LinkedIn). LinkedIn is the only ad library with Calendly ads listed (9, not all current), Meta and Google show none in the US, and Statsig's experiment SDK loads on every captured page.
